17d3im6: What does a 90% retention goal mean?

1dwedwo: 10–20 is reasonable. Each new word generates about 5-8 reviews in the first month, so learning a lot will rack up your reviews. Adjust new words per day and review session limit in Settings.
8w9iab: What is the difference between “Hard” and “Again”?
1lzsan3: “Again” = you couldn’t remember → the card returns to the learning stage (1 min) and its stability drops. “Difficult” = you remembered with effort → the interval increases only a little. Answer honestly – FSRS uses this to create the best schedule for you.
1oqkuzp: What does a 90% retention target mean?
2ck013: When a word comes up for review, you have about a 90% chance of remembering it. Increasing it to 95% makes the memory stronger, but almost doubles its ratings; lowering it to 85% means fewer reviews. 90% is the recommended balance.
1xxsjed: What if I miss a few days?
18xk8vk: No problem – FSRS counts actual elapsed time. Words that you still remember after a long interval become even more spaced out; review your “Missing” words first and limit your session so you don’t get overwhelmed.
1ynclzb: Why save words with their original phrases?
1ny64q5: The original sentence shows the actual usage: what prepositions and collocations the word takes and what nuances it carries. Seeing the context again during revision helps you use the word correctly when speaking and writing – exactly what the IELTS Lexical Resource assesses.

u1k3q9: How many new words should I learn every day?
1v7qgcb: 10 to 20 is reasonable. Each new word generates about 5-8 reviews in the first month, so learning too much will pile up your reviews. Adjust the new words per day and review session limit in Settings.
eck1rd: What is the difference between “Difficult” and “Encore”?
1mcqep8: “Again” = impossible to recall it → the card returns to the learning stage (1 min) and its stability drops. “Difficult” = you recalled it with effort → the interval only lengthens a little. Answer honestly: FSRS uses this to establish the best schedule for you.
4ynz3v: What does a 90% retention goal mean?
1pnamz6: When a word is reviewed, you have about a 90% chance of remembering it. Increasing it to 95% makes memory stronger but almost doubles your reviews; lowering it to 85% means fewer reviews. 90% is the recommended balance.
1cqmjuy: What if I miss a few days?
u4dc0h: No problem – FSRS takes actual elapsed time into account. Words that you still remember after a long interval become more spaced out; Review your “Fading” words first and limit your session so you don’t get overwhelmed.
csqiun: Why save words with their original sentences?
1xog639: The original sentence shows the actual usage: what prepositions and collocations the word takes and what nuance it carries. Seeing the context again when revising helps you use the word correctly in speaking and writing – exactly what the IELTS Lexical Resource assesses.

1klkwcu: What is the difference between “Hard” and “Longer”?
du67kk: “Again” = you can't remember it → the card returns to the learning step (1 minute) and its stability decreases. “Difficult” = you remember it with difficulty → the interval only increases slightly. Answer honestly – FSRS uses this to create the best schedule for you.
1qikmrx: What does a 90% retention target mean?
4t9w3n: When a word comes up for review, you have a ~90% chance of remembering it. Increasing it to 95% makes the memory stronger but your review almost doubles; lowering it to 85% means fewer reviews. 90% is the recommended balance.
sc5pqx: What if I miss a few days?
1d8awd5: No problem – FSRS takes into account the actual elapsed time. Words that you still remember after a long delay will be spaced further apart; review your “Fading” words first and limit your sessions so you don't get overwhelmed.
2uczs0: Why keep the words in the original sentence?
3r9lx5: The original sentence shows its actual usage: which prepositions and collocations the word uses and what nuances it carries. Looking back at the context as you review helps you use the word correctly in speaking and writing – exactly as assessed by the IELTS Lexical Resource.

1g0h8bx: 10-20 is reasonable, each new term will generate around 5–8 reviews in the first month. So learning too much will make your reviews pile up. Adjust new words per day and review session limits in Settings.
jm0312: What is the difference between "hard" and "again"?
1eg1m5x: “Again” = You don't remember → The card returns to the learning stage (1 minute) and its stability decreases. “Hard” = You remember it with effort → The time interval increases only slightly. Answer honestly – FSRS uses this to create the best schedule for you.
pby4t1: What does the 90% customer retention goal mean?
cu5o3v: When a word appears to review You have about a 90% chance of remembering the word. Increasing it to 95% will make your memory stronger. But your reviews have almost doubled. Reducing to 85% means fewer reviews. 90% is the recommended balance.
1m7jks4: What if I miss a few days?
148dgb1: No problem – FSRS takes into account the actual time that has elapsed. Words that you still remember after a long gap will be spaced further apart. Check your "faded" vocabulary first and close your session so you don't feel overwhelmed.
13og6d2: Why record words with their original sentences?
5mdqvq: The original sentence shows actual usage: which prepositions and word placements are used, and where are the nuances? Looking again at the context when you review will help you use the words correctly in speaking and writing. This is exactly what IELTS Lexical Resource assesses.

1xlpp49: 10-20 is reasonable. Each new word generates about 5-8 comments in the first month, so learning too much can cause your comments to pile up. Adjust daily vocabulary and review session limits in Settings.
179vaen: What is the difference between "hard" and "again"?
1cpgz8b: "Again" = you cannot recall it → the card returns to the learning step (1 minute) and its stability decreases. "Difficult" = it took a lot of effort for you to recall → the distance only increased a little. Honest Answers – FSRS uses this to develop the best schedule for you.
cumit6: What does a 90% retention goal mean?
14plugs: When a word needs review, you have about a 90% chance of remembering it. Increasing it to 95% makes memory better but you'll have almost double the comments; lowering it to 85% means fewer comments. 90% is the recommended balance.
1am4r6h: What if I miss a few days?
1c282gy: No problem – FSRS calculates the actual time that has elapsed. Words you still remember after a long time will become more spaced out; review your "faded" words first and end your session so you don't get overwhelmed.
1azn4sk: Why should we save words and their original sentences?
1f05i7k: The original sentence shows real usage: which prepositions and collocations the word takes and what nuances it carries. Looking again at the context when revising can help you use the word correctly in speaking and writing – which is what the IELTS Vocabulary Resources assess.

3pagsm: What is the difference between 'Hard' and 'Again'?
1r3ydk1: “Again” = cannot remember → the card returns to the learning phase (1 minute) and becomes less stable. “Difficult” = Remembered with effort → The interval is only slightly increased. Answer honestly. FSRS uses this to plan a schedule that works best for you.
1fhlny9: What does the 90% retention goal mean?
1jdcg4v: When you come across a word to review, you have about a 90% chance of remembering it. Raising it to 95% makes the memory stronger, but almost doubles the reviews. Lowering it to 85% will reduce the number of reviews. 90% is the recommended balance.
t8jemp: What happens if I miss a few days?
kh2wop: No problem. FSRS calculates actual elapsed time. Words that you still remember after a long gap are farther away. Review the “fading” word first and limit your sessions to avoid becoming overwhelmed.
1v0u5ig: Why save words as original sentences?
zs2q68: The original sentence shows the actual usage - what prepositions and collocations the word takes, and what nuances it conveys. Seeing the context again when reviewing helps you use words correctly in speaking and writing. This is exactly what the IELTS Lexical Resource assesses.

15rwg70: 10-20 is reasonable. Each new word generates between 5 and 8 reviews in the first month, so learning a lot of them will build up your reviews. Set new words daily and limit your review session in settings.
2ggsa2: What is the difference between "hard" and "again"?
1hh6bcr: “Again” = you can't remember it → the card goes back to the learning step (1 minute) and its stability decreases. “Difficult” = I remembered it with effort → the time interval is only slightly longer. Answer honestly - FSRS uses this to create the best schedule for you.
1sa3hbd: What does a 90% retention goal mean?
196c0vl: When a word comes up for review, you have up to a 90% chance of remembering it. Raising it to 95% makes the memory stronger but almost doubles your ratings; Reducing it to 85% means fewer reviews. 90% is the recommended balance.
13xb12y: What if I miss a few days?
5blbf2: No problem – FSRS calculates the actual time that has passed. The words you still remember after a long gap become more distant; Review the "fade" lyrics first and then cover your session so you don't feel overwhelmed.
ku3zt: Why memorize words with their original sentences?
u6cadm: The original sentence shows the real usage: what prepositions and collocations the word takes and what nuances it carries. Seeing the context again when reviewing helps you use the word correctly in speaking and writing – which is exactly what the IELTS Lexical Resource assesses.

njs7gt: 10–20 is quite reasonable. Each new word generates about 5-8 reviews in the first month, so if you learn too many words, your reviews will accumulate. Configure the number of new words per day and the limit of checking sessions in Settings.
1l8gdb2: What is the difference between "Hard" and "Again"?
17tfup2: “Again” = you couldn’t remember → the card returns to the learning stage (1 minute) and its stability decreases. “Difficult” = you remembered with effort → the interval increases only slightly. Answer honestly - FSRS uses this to create the best schedule for you.
kmv9cj: What does a 90% retention goal mean?
165eulk: When a word comes up for repetition, you have a ~90% chance of remembering it. Increasing the value to 95% will strengthen memory, but the number of reviews will almost double; dropping it to 85% means fewer reviews. 90% is the recommended balance.
lvjvin: What if I miss a few days?
2z43fx: No problem - FSRS takes actual elapsed time into account. The words you still remember after a long time are pushed further away; review your Fade words first and limit your session to avoid becoming overwhelmed.
g6nx9h: Why save words along with their original sentences?
m73chn: The original sentence shows the actual usage: what prepositions and phrases the word takes and what nuance it carries. Again, looking at the context as you review will help you use the word correctly in speech and writing - exactly what the IELTS vocabulary resource assesses.

1yedemk: What is the difference between "Hard" and "Again"?
tjqmsy: "Again" = you couldn't remember → the card goes back to the learning step (1 minute) and its stability decreases. “Hardly” = you remembered with effort → the interval is only slightly longer. Answer honestly – FSRS uses this to create the best program for you.
1ra3p8z: What does a 90% retention goal mean?
1co1pl5: When a word comes up for review, you have a ~90% chance of remembering it. Raising this to 95% improves memory but nearly doubles your reviews; Lowering it to 85% means fewer comments. 90% is the recommended balance.
15t7bek: What if I miss a few days?
1nag7h5: No problem – FSRS takes into account the actual elapsed time. The words you still remember after a long time become even more spaced; Review your “Fade” words first and limit your session to avoid getting overwhelmed.
izqu5j: Why keep words with their original sentences?
cmlixa: The original sentence shows actual usage: what prepositions and collocations the word takes and what nuance it carries. Seeing the context again as you review helps you use the word correctly in speaking and writing; This is exactly what the IELTS Lexical Resource evaluates.

pijmw6: Recipient name unknown: Dear Sir or Madam → Yours faithfully. Known Names: Dear Mr/Ms + Last Name → Yours sincerely. No abbreviations or slang.
12m6qhz: People you know but are not close to (neighbours, landlords, co-workers): Dear Mr/Ms + last name → Kind regards / Best regards. Polite but natural.
1wjir87: Friends and Family: Dear/Hi + First Name → Best wishes / Love / See you soon. Contractions (I'm, can't) and exclamation points are fine.
6f9ern: Contractions should be avoided in formal letters (found, e.g. I'm, can't).
